extract:
Kendrick Lamar Duckworth was born in 1987 in Compton, California, and emerged from the same West Coast lineage that produced N.W.A., Dr. Dre, and Snoop Dogg — artists he grew up idolizing, having reportedly witnessed the filming of the "California Love" video as a child. He began releasing mixtapes as a teenager under the name K-Dot in the mid-2000s, eventually signing to Carson-based independent label Top Dawg Entertainment (TDE), the home base that would shape his entire career. By 2010 he had dropped the K-Dot moniker and released the Kendrick Lamar EP, signaling a more introspective, autobiographical turn.

His 2011 independent album Section.80, featuring tracks like "HiiiPoWeR" and "A.D.H.D.," established him as a generational voice and earned the attention of Dr. Dre, who signed him to Aftermath and Interscope in a joint deal with TDE. The 2012 follow-up good kid, m.A.A.d city — billed as "a short film by Kendrick Lamar" — was a coming-of-age concept record set against Compton gang life, anchored by singles "Swimming Pools (Drank)," "Backseat Freestyle," and "Bitch, Don't Kill My Vibe." It went multi-platinum and cemented him alongside Drake and J. Cole as the defining rapper of his cohort, particularly after his combative verse on Big Sean's "Control" in 2013.

In 2015 Lamar released To Pimp a Butterfly, a sprawling work steeped in jazz, funk, and spoken word, with contributions from Thundercat, Kamasi Washington, Flying Lotus, Robert Glasper, Pharrell, and producer Sounwave. Tracks like "Alright" became a protest anthem during the Black Lives Matter movement, while "King Kunta" and "The Blacker the Berry" pushed his lyricism into more overtly political territory. He followed it with the compilation untitled unmastered. in 2016, then DAMN. in 2017, a tighter, more radio-facing record featuring "HUMBLE.," "DNA.," and "LOYALTY." with Rihanna. DAMN. won the Pulitzer Prize for Music in 2018, the first non-classical, non-jazz work to do so. That same year he curated and largely performed on the Black Panther soundtrack alongside SZA, Future, and other TDE artists.

After a lengthy hiatus, Lamar returned in 2022 with Mr. Morale & The Big Steppers, a double album dealing with therapy, generational trauma, and personal accountability, featuring "N95," "Father Time" with Sampha, and "United in Grief." He subsequently parted ways with Top Dawg Entertainment after fulfilling his contract and launched pgLang, a creative company co-founded with longtime collaborator Dave Free. In 2024 he engaged in a high-profile public feud with Drake, releasing the diss tracks "Like That" (with Future and Metro Boomin), "Euphoria," and "Not Like Us," the last of which became a chart-topping cultural phenomenon and earned multiple Grammys. Later that year he surprise-released the album GNX.

Lamar is widely regarded as one of the most acclaimed rappers of his era, with multiple Grammy wins, the aforementioned Pulitzer, and a reputation as a meticulous lyricist and conceptualist.
